chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the urine of the infant. He said: “Pour water over it; but if he has already eaten, then wash it thoroughly. And the boy and the girl are equal in rule.”

So this does not conflict with the first report, because the first report only negated washing the garment from it in the manner that it is washed from the urine of an adult man, or from his urine after he has eaten food, and it did not negate that water be poured over it. The ruling of the girl’s urine is not like that, because her urine must necessarily be washed. And his statement, “the boy and the girl are equal in rule,” means after eating food, and this is also indicated by that.

key_terms.بَوْلِ الصَّبِيِّ: the urine of an infant child
key_terms.تَصُبُّ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ: water is poured over it for purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cleaning infant urine in Shi'a fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on the urine of an infant and distinguishes between the case before and after the child begins eating food. It also addresses how earlier reports are to be reconciled, clarifying the legal ruling regarding purification of clothing affected by such urine.
